**Final Information**  
**Page:** *Marie of Romania* – https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania  
**Evidence:** [P116] [P118] [P154]  
**Coverage:** The page confirms the subject’s blue eyes, her marriage while living outside her birth country, and the death of her youngest child.  
**Missing:**  
- Evidence that she never drank alcohol.  
- The letter requesting people to bring flowers to the child’s resting place.  
**Next links:**  
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Mircea_of_Romania – (to investigate the circumstances of the child’s death and any related correspondence)  
**Expand:** yes – the current excerpts do not provide information on alcohol abstention or the flower‑letter, so further navigation is needed for those facts.  
**Status:** partial

source_blocks.P116: Marie grew into a "lovely young woman" with "sparkling blue eyes and silky fair hair"; she was courted by several royal bachelors, including [Prince George of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_V "George V"), who in 1892 became second in line to inherit the throne.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200531-37)[Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"), the [Prince of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_VII "Edward VII"), and Marie's father the [Duke of Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred,_Duke_of_Saxe-Coburg_and_Gotha "Alfred, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha") all approved, but the [Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_of_Denmark "Alexandra of Denmark"), and Marie's mother, the [Duchess of Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Duchess_Maria_Alexandrovna_of_Russia "Grand Duchess Maria Alexandrovna of Russia") did not. The Princess of Wales disapproved of the family's pro-German sentiment, while the Duchess of Edinburgh did not wish her daughter to remain in England, which she disliked. In addition, the Princess of Wales (whose father, [Christian IX of Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_IX_of_Denmark "Christian IX of Denmark"), had been a minor German prince before being called to the Danish throne) was higher than Marie in the [order of precedence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_precedence_in_England_and_Wales "Order of precedence in England and Wales").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPope-Hennessy1959250%E2%80%9351-38) The Duchess of Edinburgh was also opposed to marriage between first cousins, which was not allowed by her native Russian Orthodox Church.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMandache2001334-39) Thus, when George proposed to her, Marie informed him that the marriage was impossible and that he must remain her "beloved chum". Queen Victoria would later comment that "Georgie lost Missy by waiting & waiting".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200532-40)
source_blocks.P118: On 10 January 1893, Marie and Ferdinand were married at [Sigmaringen Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmaringen_Castle "Sigmaringen Castle").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPakula198468-45) During the evening before the wedding, Marie's father [Prince Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred,_Duke_of_Saxe-Coburg_and_Gotha "Alfred, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha") reportedly summoned Marie to his rooms to inform her that he and her mother had settled a dowry of 1,000,000 French francs[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPakula198467-46) (then worth approximately £40,000)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-EdvinssonEtAl2010-47) on Marie, before bursting into tears and declaring that he had hoped for a different destiny for his daughter.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPakula198467-46) The couple were married in three ceremonies: one civil, one Catholic (Ferdinand's religion) and one Anglican. The civil ceremony was performed in the Red Hall of the castle by Karl von Wendel, the [German Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_II,_German_Emperor "Wilhelm II, German Emperor") being the first of the witnesses present to sign the marriage act. At four o'clock, the Catholic ceremony took place at the Town Church, with Marie being led to the altar by her father. The Anglican ceremony was more modest and was conducted in one of the chambers of the castle.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-48)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPakula198468-45) Although King Carol granted the couple "_Honigtag_" (one day of honeymoon), Marie and Ferdinand spent a few days at the Castle of [Krauchenwies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krauchenwies "Krauchenwies") in Bavaria. From there, they left for the countryside, interrupting their journey briefly to stop at [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), where they visited [Emperor Franz Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Franz_Joseph "Emperor Franz Joseph"). Due to growing tensions between Austria and Romania (the visit took place during the ongoing movement of the [Transylvanian Memorandum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvanian_Memorandum "Transylvanian Memorandum")), the couple's visit was brief, and they arrived in the border town of [Predeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predeal "Predeal") following a nighttime crossing of Transylvania by train.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarie_1991,_Vol_210%E2%80%9314-49) Marie was warmly welcomed by the Romanian people, who were longing for a more personal monarchy.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGauthier201052-50)
source_blocks.P154: On 2 November 1916, Marie's youngest son, Prince Mircea, who had been sick with [typhoid fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid_fever "Typhoid fever"), died at [Buftea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buftea "Buftea"). Marie was distraught and wrote in her journal: "Can anything ever be the same?"[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-105) After [Bucharest fell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Bucharest "Battle of Bucharest") to Austrian troops, the royal court was transferred to [Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i "Iași"), capital of the [Moldavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Moldavia "Western Moldavia") region, in December 1916.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-odnb-22) There, she continued to act as a nurse in military hospitals. Daily, Marie would dress as a nurse and go to [the train station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_railway_station "Iași railway station"), where she would receive more injured soldiers; then she would transport them to hospital.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTESaint-Aulaire1953360-106)

The Princess of Wales disapproved of the family's pro-German sentiment, while the Duchess of Edinburgh did not wish her daughter to remain in England, which she disliked. In addition, the Princess of Wales (whose father, [Christian IX of Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_IX_of_Denmark "Christian IX of Denmark"), had been a minor German prince before being called to the Danish throne) was higher than Marie in the [order of precedence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_precedence_in_England_and_Wales "Order of precedence in England and Wales").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPope-Hennessy1959250%E2%80%9351-38) The Duchess of Edinburgh was also opposed to marriage between first cousins, which was not allowed by her native Russian Orthodox Church.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMandache2001334-39) Thus, when George proposed to her, Marie informed him that the marriage was impossible and that he must remain her "beloved chum". Queen Victoria would later comment that "Georgie lost Missy by waiting & waiting".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200532-40)
source_blocks.P117: Around this time, King [Carol I of Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_I_of_Romania "Carol I of Romania") was looking for a suitable bride for his nephew, [Crown Prince Ferdinand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Romania "Ferdinand I of Romania"), in order to secure the succession and ensure the continuation of the [House of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen "House of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen"). Possibly motivated by the prospect of removing tensions between Russia and Romania on the subject of control over [Bessarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bessarabia "Bessarabia"), the Duchess of Edinburgh suggested that Marie meet Ferdinand.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMandache2001334-39) Marie and Ferdinand first became acquainted during a [gala](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/gala "wikt:gala") dinner, where they conversed in German. She found him shy but amiable, and their second meeting went just as well.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200533-41) Once they were formally engaged, Queen Victoria wrote to another granddaughter, [Princess Victoria of Hesse and by Rhine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Victoria_of_Hesse_and_by_Rhine "Princess Victoria of Hesse and by Rhine"), that "[Ferdinand] is nice & the Parents are charming–but the country is very insecure & the immorality of the Society at Bucharest quite awful. Of course the marriage will be delayed some time as Missy won't be 17 till the end of October!"[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200534-42)[German Empress Frederick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empress_Frederick "German Empress Frederick"), Marie's aunt, wrote to her daughter, [Crown Princess Sophia of Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Princess_Sophia_of_Greece "Crown Princess Sophia of Greece"), that "Missy is till now quite delighted, but the poor child is so young, how can she guess what is before her?"[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelardi200535-43) In late 1892, King Carol visited London in order to meet the Duke of Edinburgh and Queen Victoria, who eventually agreed to the marriage and appointed him a [Knight of the Garter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_of_the_Garter "Knight of the Garter").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_of_Romania#cite_note-FOOTNOTEElsberry197244-44)

source_blocks.P43: Since September, the wetland has held the status of **Nature Sanctuary** , reflecting its value and fragility. The town of Carrizal Bajo is accessible by car, but the wetland itself must be explored on foot, taking care to stay on the marked trails. Its proximity to **Llanos de Challe National Park** (just 3,5 km away) facilitates routes that combine coastline, the flowering desert during rainy years, and conservation efforts—a perfect opportunity to promote joint protection initiatives.
source_blocks.P61: South of the city of Caldera, on the Atacama coast, the mouth of the **Copiapó River** is a true oasis: coastal lagoons surrounded by dense reed beds where hundreds of birds nest and rest, and where foxes and small native rodents also roam. Since 2022, its 115,2 hectares have been officially protected as a **Nature Sanctuary** , a landmark designation that recognizes its ecological importance in an arid environment.
